title: Roasted Cherry Tomato Pasta
subtitle: Slow-roasted cherry tomatoes blitzed into a silky pasta sauce
excerpt: Cherry tomatoes and garlic roast together until jammy and sweet, then get roughly crushed into a glossy sauce for spaghetti. A handful of basil and Parmesan finish the dish.
sourceNotes: Roasting concentrates tomatoes far more than a quick pan sauce can. The technique is widely used across southern Italian cooking and has become a home-cook staple for its simplicity.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the tomatoes ahead and keep in the fridge for up to three days. Warm through before tossing with fresh pasta.

content.text: Use a high-sided roasting tin to prevent the tomato juices from scorching on the oven floor.
Tip the cherry tomatoes and garlic cloves into the roasting tin. Drizzle with 4 tablespoons of olive oil. Season with salt and scatter over the chilli flakes.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until the tomatoes have burst and the edges are lightly charred.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in a large pot of well-salted boiling water. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
Squeeze the roasted garlic from its skins into the tin. Crush the tomatoes roughly with a fork.
Add the drained pasta to the tin. Toss well, adding pasta water a little at a time to loosen the sauce.
Drizzle over the remaining olive oil. Tear in the basil and toss once more.
Serve with Parmesan grated over the top.

items.symptom: Tomatoes are not jammy after 35 minutes.
items.cause: Tomatoes were very large or the oven runs cool.
items.fix: Return to the oven for 10 more minutes; halve any large ones first.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thin and watery.
items.cause: Tomatoes released a lot of juice.
items.fix: Pour off excess liquid before adding the pasta.

items.symptom: Pasta clumps when added to the tin.
items.cause: Not enough pasta water to emulsify the oil.
items.fix: Add pasta water gradually while tossing continuously.
